summary.text: Mike Kelly is the Republican incumbent for Pennsylvania's 16th District. A Butler, Pennsylvania auto dealer who served on the Butler School Board and Butler City Council, he was first elected to Congress in 2010 and sits on the Ways and Means Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Tax. He is seeking re-election in 2026.

paragraphs.text: Kelly was born in Pittsburgh in 1948 and raised in Butler, Pennsylvania, where, according to his official biography, he has lived for more than 50 years.
He graduated from Butler High School in 1966 and attended the University of Notre Dame on a football and academic scholarship, earning a bachelor's degree in 1970.

After college he returned to Butler to work at Kelly Chevrolet-Cadillac, a dealership his father founded in the early 1950s; he took ownership in the mid-1990s and added Hyundai and Kia franchises, according to his official biography.

Kelly served on the Butler School Board from 1992 to 1995 and on the Butler City Council from 2006 to 2009, and he also sat on the boards of local civic bodies including the Housing Authority and Redevelopment Authority of Butler County.

According to his official biography, he decided to run for Congress in 2009 after a General Motors restructuring threatened his dealership's Cadillac franchise; he went to arbitration and won, and ran for Congress the following year.
He was first elected in 2010 and sworn in on January 5, 2011, initially for Pennsylvania's 3rd District, and he has represented the 16th District since January 3, 2019.
Kelly serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and, per his official page, chairs its Subcommittee on Tax; Ballotpedia also lists him on the committee's Health Subcommittee.

His official biography lists him as Republican chair of several caucuses, including the Congressional Korea Caucus, the House Automotive Caucus and the Childhood Cancer Caucus, and as an appointed member of the President's Export Council.

The biography says he and his wife, Victoria, a former elementary school teacher, have four children and ten grandchildren, and that he founded the Butler Quarterback Club and the Golden Tornado Scholastic Foundation, which provide educational programs in the Butler Area School District.
